what_its_for: Clonazepam is used to help control seizures (epilepsy) and to treat panic disorder, which includes sudden feelings of intense fear or discomfort. It belongs to a group of medicines called benzodiazepines, which work by calming activity in the brain and nervous system.
how_to_take: Take clonazepam exactly as your doctor tells you to. Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. You can take it with or without food. If you use the orally disintegrating tablet (ODT), place it on your tongue and let it dissolve — do not chew or swallow it whole. Never take more than prescribed, and do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious withdrawal symptoms.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time. For seizures, adults usually start at 0.5 mg taken 3 times a day. For panic disorder, adults usually start at 0.25 mg taken twice a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond to the medicine. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — your dose may be different from what is listed here.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store clonazepam at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a secure location out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a safe medication take-back program near you.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking clonazepam — it can cause dangerous increases in drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, muscle relaxers, narcotic pain medicines, or other anxiety medications, unless your doctor approves. Do not start or stop any other medications without first talking to your doctor or pharmacist.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: thoughts of harming yourself or suicide, new or worsening depression or anxiety, unusual mood or behavior changes, trouble breathing or slow breathing, severe drowsiness or confusion, signs of an allergic reaction (rash, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing), or if your seizures get worse. Also contact your doctor if you feel dependent on the medication or have strong urges to take more than prescribed.
when_it_works: Clonazepam starts working fairly quickly, usually within 1 to 4 hours after taking a dose. For panic disorder, it may take a few days to a couple of weeks before you notice the full benefit. For seizure control, your doctor will monitor how well it is working and may adjust your dose. Keep taking your medicine as prescribed even if you feel better.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older) are more sensitive to clonazepam and may be at higher risk for falls, confusion, and memory problems — lower doses are usually used. Pregnant women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as it may harm an unborn baby. Clonazepam passes into breast milk and may cause drowsiness or feeding problems in a nursing baby — discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Children can use clonazepam for seizures, but doses are carefully calculated based on body weight by the doctor.
